task: Add --claude-desktop, --vscode, and --vscode-claude-code disconnect flags mirroring the existing --codex-desktop reference implementation, extending disconnect-orchestrator.ts to four-target dispatch with per-target success/failure reporting.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches 5 files across 2-3 layers: CLI (index.ts flag declarations), orchestrator (disconnect-orchestrator.ts extending single-target DISCONNECT_TARGET_LIST to four with a new per-target result/summary shape), and 3 connector files (desktop.ts, vscode.ts, vscode-claude-code.ts) each needing a new exported removal function alongside its existing write function. Shared utilities (writeAtomically, ConfigurationError, getCodemiePath marker-file convention) are reused rather than invented.

Core flow is clear and mirrors an existing implementation, but the ticket text leaves several open design decisions unresolved per the technical analysis's Risk Indicators: no --insiders equivalent for the two VS Code disconnect targets, whether Claude Desktop's non-MCP inferenceProvider/gatewayKey top-level keys should also be cleared, no backup-fallback mechanism defined for the three new targets if structural removal fails to cleanly identify CodeMie's entries, and desktop.ts's marker-read/write helpers being module-private today. These are design decisions to be settled in spec/plan, not just wiring.

The 4th target (codex-desktop) is an exact, working precedent for the orchestrator/CLI wiring and error-reporting contract, which lowers novelty. But no exact precedent exists for Claude Desktop's specific removal logic (reading a currently-private managedNames marker and re-running reconcileManagedMcpServers with an empty managed set through the _meta.json/appliedId indirection), and none of the three new targets has a backup-fallback the way codex-desktop's .codemie-backup does — a rollback plan is needed if structural removal misses entries.

5 files modified in src/ (index.ts, disconnect-orchestrator.ts, desktop.ts, vscode.ts, vscode-claude-code.ts) plus the existing disconnect-orchestrator.test.ts needing restructuring (not just additions, since the target set and reporting shape change), plus ~3 new test files for the three new removal functions (no existing removal test coverage for any of them) — spanning 4 directories (src/cli/commands/proxy/, connectors/, and their respective __tests__/ subdirectories).

red_flags_applied: Requirements Clarity bumped from L (4) to XL (5): the technical analysis's Risk Indicators section lists multiple unresolved design questions the ticket text does not address — the missing --insiders selector for VS Code disconnect targets, whether Claude Desktop's non-MCP inferenceProvider/gatewayKey keys should be cleared alongside managedMcpServers, and the absence of any backup-fallback mechanism for the three new targets.
